newsitem.title: USA: UBS analyst sees continued U.S. bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: UBS analyst sees continued U.S. bank mergers.

text.p: UBS Securities' analyst Thomas Hanley told an investment conference Thursday he expects the wave of U.S. bank mergers to continue.
He said his top five merger candidates were First American Corp, First Commerce Corp, First of America, Signet Banking, and Union Planters Corp.
Hanley also said a merger between Citicorp and American Express Co was a possibility. "Maybe it happens, maybe it does not," he said.
Hanley said he expects the net charge-off ratio in the U.S. credit card business to peak at 7.25 percent in the first quarter of 1998. The rate is about 6.40 percent currently.

Hanley said he expects U.S. bank stocks to bounce back in 1997 from recent losses and test highs reached earlier this year. He said he expects the economy to moderate this year and sees growth picking up in the second half of 1998 which will create a more challenging environment in 1999.
He also said he expects bank stocks to be in the "third wave" of an investment cycle in 1999. He said the third wave is a time when bank stocks should be sold.
